newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian troops foil carnage, kill rebels - paper.
newsitem.headline: Algerian troops foil carnage, kill rebels - paper.

text.p: Algerian troops, tipped off about an impending attack, moved ahead of Moslem rebels to a village and thwarted an attempt to carry out a massacre, an Algerian newspaper said on Monday.
The soldiers shot dead two rebels and wounded three as a group of about 30 moved into the village south of Algiers at the weekend, Liberte newspaper said.
The rest fled into mountains around the village near Larba, 25 km (15 miles) from the Algerian capital.

The military success was reported amid bitter questioning by opposition party leaders and ordinary Algerians on how rebels have been able to slaughter scores of villagers in hamlets, some close to army barracks and other paramilitary posts.

Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia came under fire from some opposition deputies at the weekend over that security issue as he presented his programme before the National Assembly (lower house) in which 10 political parties and 11 independents are represented.

More than 700 civilians, mostly villagers in remote hamlets, have been slaughtered by having their throats cut, heads chopped off, shot dead or burned alive in the past two months in attacks the authorities blame on Moslem guerrillas.
About 60,000 people have died in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
